description: Communicative-function codebook for official live-service game patch notes. The LLM is used as a coding instrument. It labels a target text while receiving limited, explicit local context.
unit_of_analysis: One target text item. Target items are produced by deterministic segmentation: stat/list rows stay intact, headings become context, and long prose blocks are split into sentence-level or short paragraph-level targets. Only target_text receives a label and only target_text words are counted in aggregation.
context_policy: The model may use section_heading, context_before, and context_after only to understand the target_text. It must not label the context itself.

change_documentation.label: Change documentation
change_documentation.description: Text that records what changed, what was added, removed, adjusted, or fixed.

developer_intent_communication.label: Developer-intent communication
developer_intent_communication.description: Text that makes developer reasoning, audience relationship, or future monitoring visible.

other_context.label: Other/context
other_context.description: Text retained for auditability but excluded from the two main metrics.

global_instructions: Use context_before, context_after, and section_heading only to disambiguate the target_text.
Do not label the context fields themselves.
Do not infer internal developer intent beyond what is visibly communicated in the text.
Choose exactly one primary_label from the codebook.
Use secondary_labels only if a second communicative function is clearly present in target_text.
If the target is only a heading, navigation fragment, isolated name, or unclear fragment, use non_substantive.

change_specification.label: Change specification
change_specification.description: The target specifies what changed, was added, removed, adjusted, enabled, disabled, restricted, or reworked. This includes numerical stat rows, gameplay rules, system changes, feature changes, policy restrictions, and compact changelog bullets.
positive_examples: Attack Speed: 35% → 33%
Maximum party size: 2 players → 4 players
Third-party sites may not share augment win rates
negative_examples: We want this item to better serve fighters
We will keep an eye on how this lands
Fixed a bug where the tooltip showed the wrong value

corrective_maintenance.label: Corrective maintenance
corrective_maintenance.description: The target describes fixing a bug, crash, exploit, typo, tooltip, visual issue, audio issue, UI issue, or other unintended behavior.
positive_examples: Fixed a bug where the ability sometimes failed to cast
Corrected a tooltip that displayed the wrong damage value
Resolved a crash that could occur when loading into a match
negative_examples: Damage: 60 → 70
We are changing this because it was too frustrating
New skins will be available this week

design_rationale.label: Design rationale
design_rationale.description: The target explains why a change was made, what problem it addresses, what design goal it serves, what tradeoff is being made, or what effect the developers expect.
positive_examples: We want this rune to be a riskier late-game option
This should preserve the champion's identity while reducing burst
Our goal is to make Arena encourage experimentation rather than fixed scripts
negative_examples: Cooldown: 12 → 10 seconds
Fixed a bug where the item triggered twice
Prestige skin available June 12

audience_engagement.label: Audience engagement
audience_engagement.description: The target directly addresses players, readers, the community, partners, testers, feedback, reports, PBE, survey responses, or shared expectations. Mentions of players as in-game actors do not count unless the text is engaging the audience or their feedback.
positive_examples: Thanks for all the feedback on this change
We know many of you have been asking for this
We want to make sure partners are aware of this policy
negative_examples: Players gain 20 gold on takedown
This champion has many expert players
Attack Speed: 35% → 33%

future_monitoring.label: Future monitoring
future_monitoring.description: The target frames a change as provisional, experimental, or subject to future monitoring, iteration, follow-up, tuning, or later communication.
positive_examples: We will be keeping a close eye on how the meta develops
We may make further adjustments in a future patch
We'll monitor this change and follow up if needed
negative_examples: Damage: 20 → 25
We changed this to improve early lane clarity
Fixed a bug where the item could be duplicated

promotional_context.label: Promotional/contextual framing
promotional_context.description: The target promotes or frames events, skins, battle passes, cosmetics, esports, lore, marketing beats, external videos/blogs, or other non-balance context.
positive_examples: New skins will be available on July 31
Welcome to our summer event
Watch the full Dev Update for more details
negative_examples: Q damage decreased
We are changing this because it was unhealthy
Fixed a tooltip issue

non_substantive.label: Non-substantive/unclear
non_substantive.description: The target is a heading, isolated name, navigation text, repeated title, link fragment, table artifact, or too unclear to classify substantively.
positive_examples: Bugfixes & QoL Changes
Trinity Force
Read more here
negative_examples: Attack Speed: 35% → 33%
Fixed a bug where the tooltip was wrong
We will monitor this change closely
